events.title: The death of St. Finian of Clonard
events.shortBlurb: The master of Clonard, from whose school went out the Twelve Apostles of Erin, died on 12 December, mourned as the tutor of the saints of Ireland…
body: A native of Leinster, instructed in the faith by disciples of St. Patrick, Finian passed into Wales, where he conversed with St. David, St. Gildas, and St. Cathmael, and after some thirty years in Britain returned to Ireland about the year 520, excellently qualified, as Butler says, by sanctity and sacred learning.

He founded many monasteries and schools, the chief at Cluain-Eraird — Eraird's Meadow — now Clonard in Meath, which became a famous seminary; his Irish life reckons three thousand scholars. Out of his school came Kiaran the Younger, Columkille, Columba the son of Crimthain, the two Brendans, Laserian, Canicus, and Ruadan — the twelve whom old Irish writers name the Twelve Apostles of Erin — and their master was called the tutor of the saints of Ireland.

Chosen and consecrated bishop of Clonard, he lived on bread and herbs, drank water, and slept on the ground with a stone for his pillow. He died on 12 December, of the yellow plague as is commonly said; the year is reckoned as 549 by modern writers and as 552 by the Annals of Inisfallen.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 12 December
Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Apostles of Erin, The Twelve”
